Application Requirements, Deadlines & Process
Applications must be submitted through the graduate admissions portal based on the starting semester.
Spring, Summer, or Fall 2027
If you’re a first-time user, make a new account with your email and password. If you are a current Lehigh undergraduate student accessing the graduate application for the first time, select the “Forgot Your Password?” link to reactivate your account using your Lehigh email address.
Important Information
Uploaded transcripts are not considered official. All applicants who accept an admissions offer must submit final, official transcripts through past educational institutions.
Most of our programs are GMAT/GRE-optional. If you are unsure whether you need to take either test, please refer to your program’s admissions page.
International students whose native language is not English must demonstrate their English language proficiency by providing an official letter showing completion of an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited college or university where the primary medium of instruction was English. This can also be fulfilled by reporting your unofficial TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo test scores and later sending your official test report to Lehigh.
After you submit your application, a confirmation email will be sent to the email address you provided in your application.
If you’re having issues logging in or submitting your application, please check our FAQs below or contact us via graduateadmissionshelp@lehigh.edu. In your email, please include your full name, address, and date of birth as provided in your application.
Application Tips
Begin the process early to allow yourself enough time to navigate the program selection and application.
Verify your application for accuracy and completion, ensuring all necessary items have been included. Upon submission of your application, graduate admissions staff will do a preliminary review of your application. Contact information can be found in your application portal.
Admissions to Lehigh’s graduate programs are coordinated by each college, but a summary of the university’s criteria and related admissions information can be found in the course catalog.
Keep track of deadlines and consider sending in your application days or even weeks ahead of time.
Application Deadlines
Graduate program deadlines vary based on the department and program. Please refer to your college’s website for program-specific details.

Frequently Asked Questions
Program of Study Questions
Where can I get information about the programs and graduate degrees at Lehigh?
Lehigh University has more than 85 programs to choose from, including research-based doctoral programs, professional and research-based master's degree and certificate programs. For many programs, we offer both residential and online options, as well as full-time or part-time courses, to meet students’ needs. There are many ways you can learn more about the different options available.
If you know the type of program you are interested in, you can begin to find information about it on our Graduate Programs page.
If you know which of Lehigh’s five colleges you are interested in joining, you can begin on our Graduate Admissions page.
Do you have online programs?
Lehigh offers online and hybrid options in many programs:
Hybrid and online programs in the P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science can be seen on the Master's Programs in Engineering page, or inquire at engineering@lehigh.edu.
If you are interested in fully online programs in the College of Education, please visit the College of Education Degree & Certification Explorer page.
For the College of Health, inquire by contacting cohgrad@lehigh.edu or checking out the College of Health Graduate Programs page.
Hybrid and online programs in the College of Business can be found on the College of Business Graduate Programs page, or inquire at business@lehigh.edu.
Can I apply to more than one program? And more than one college?
Yes, students may apply to more than one program and/or more than one college. However, for each separate program, a new application (and application fee, as applicable) will be required.
General Application Questions
How do I access the application?
The Lehigh graduate application can be found on the Graduate Admissions page.
I am having trouble with the application portal, who can I contact?
Please email graduateadmissionshelp@lehigh.edu. Note that the turnaround time for a response to your question may be 24-48 hours, depending upon the time of year and email volume.
I submitted my application, but realized I made an error. How can I correct it?
Once your application has been submitted, contact the College to make any updates or correct any errors.

Can I add additional documents to my application after I’ve submitted my application? (Ex. updated test scores, updated transcripts, updated references, updated projects/research/publications)
If your application has not yet been submitted, you may log into the application portal and change the information directly. If you have submitted your application, you are not able to edit this information yourself. Please contact the department and/or college office for assistance. In the case of updated test scores or transcripts, have these sent directly to Lehigh.
Can I defer my admission to a different semester?
Yes, students are allowed to defer their admission to a graduate program at Lehigh for up to one year. If your program requires a deposit, the deposit must be paid to request deferral. You should request deferral prior to the 5th day of the academic semester you originally applied for (2nd day of Summer II for Summer start programs). See the academic calendar for the specific dates. Contact your college office for your deferral options.
What are the requirements to apply?
Each college has their own application requirements. In most cases, the following minimum requirements are needed:
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
Academic Transcripts
English Language Proficiency
Resume
Personal statement
Letters of recommendation
Some programs require entrance exams (GRE, etc.)
For more information, see the following pages:

If my program doesn’t specify what to include in my personal statement, what should I write about?
If a program doesn’t provide specific prompts, your personal statement should tell a cohesive story that connects your past achievements to your future goals. Focus on the four core pillars of a strong graduate statement:
Your "Why": Explain your motivation for pursuing this specific field. What sparked your interest, and how has that passion evolved?
Your Preparation: Highlight relevant academic background, research experience, internships, or professional work that proves you are ready for graduate-level rigor.
Why This Program: Demonstrate fit. Mention specific faculty members you want to work with, unique labs, or curriculum features that align with your goals, whichever is appropriate to the type of program you are pursuing.
Future Goals: Clearly state what you plan to do with this degree after graduation and how this specific program acts as the launchpad for those career aspirations.
When can I expect to receive a decision?
Each college has their own processing timelines, which are often closely linked to the application deadlines.
Most PhD applications are processed between December and February for fall admissions.
Master’s applications in the College of Business, the College of Health, and the College of Engineering are often processed on a rolling basis. Some Master’s applications in the College of Arts & Sciences are processed on a rolling basis as well.
I would like to withdraw my application, can my application fee be refunded?
We do not refund application fees.
Recommendation Letter Questions
My recommender didn't get the email to submit a recommendation, what do I do?
First, we suggest that the recommender check their spam folder. It is not uncommon for recommendation requests to be flagged as spam. If the message is not visible, you may contact gradadmissionshelp@lehigh.edu, and they can resend the reminder directly or provide you with alternate instructions on how to ensure your recommendation is properly received and filed.

Do my recommenders get notified for their LOR request?
Yes. Your recommender should receive an automated notification from the graduate application system. As with many application systems, these notices can occasionally be identified as spam. If your recommender does not receive it, please ask that they check their spam filter. If they continue to experience issues, please contact your college at the address below.

How do I change my recommender’s contact information?
If your application has not yet been submitted, you may log into the application portal and change the information directly. If you have submitted your application, you are not able to edit this information yourself. Please contact the department and/or college office for assistance.
Can I remove or replace one of my listed recommenders?
If your application has not yet been submitted, you may log into the application portal and change the information directly. Please note that recommenders are contacted as soon as you click “Send request”. As such, if you choose to change your recommender, there may be some confusion. If you have submitted your application, you are not able to edit this information yourself. Please contact the department and/or college office for assistance.
How do I add or change a recommender?
If your application has not yet been submitted, you may log into the application portal and change the information directly. Please note that recommenders are contacted as soon as you click “Send request”. As such, if you choose to change your recommender, there may be some confusion on the part of the recommender who has already received the request. If you have submitted your application, you are not able to edit this information yourself. Please contact the department and/or college office for assistance.
Who should I ask to write a recommendation letter?
Recommendation forms should be submitted by individuals qualified to evaluate the applicant’s academic achievements and potential for graduate studies. In most cases, recommendations from professors are preferred. However, letters from employers, supervisors, or professional associates are accepted, especially if your program of study requires work experience.
Test Score Questions
What if I am unable to sit for the required/recommended standardized tests before the application deadline?
We encourage all applicants to submit application materials by the application deadline. However, there is a short grace period allowed within each college. If your materials are not immediately available, please try to submit them within seven business days of submitting your application.
Arts & Sciences: We encourage all applicants to have all application materials submitted by the applicable deadline. Please be aware that we accept unofficial transcripts and test scores in order for an application to be considered ready to review. Typically, applicants will have one to two weeks after the application deadline for remaining materials to arrive. This may vary depending on the program.
Lehigh Business: While we encourage all applicants to have all application materials submitted by an application deadline, typically COB applicants will have around seven to ten days after the application deadline for remaining application materials to arrive, such as GRE, TOEFL, Duolingo, etc. This may vary depending on the program and if an applicant is applying from outside of the United States.
Education: While we encourage all COE applicants to have all application materials submitted by an application deadline, typically COE applicants will have five to seven days after the application deadline for remaining application materials to arrive, such as TOEFL, IELTS, etc. This may vary depending on the program.
Rossin College: We encourage all applicants to have all application materials submitted by the applicable deadline. Please be aware that we accept unofficial transcripts and test scores in order for an application to be considered ready to review. Typically, applicants will have one to two weeks after the application deadline for remaining materials to arrive. This may vary depending on the program.
Health: Applicants are strongly encouraged to have all their application materials submitted by the listed application deadline. Please be aware that we accept unofficial transcripts and test scores in order for an application to be considered ready to review. Typically, applicants will have one to two weeks after the application deadline for remaining materials to arrive.This may vary depending on the program.
Is GRE/GMAT required?
Most programs at Lehigh do not require a GRE or GMAT for admission consideration. It is best to review the policies of the specific college and/or program to determine the application requirements for the program of interest.

What if my English language test scores don’t meet the minimum requirement for the program I’m applying to?
In some programs, students may be admitted to the program of interest with additional requirements. Students might be required to complete StepUp prior to matriculation or take EAPC courses during their first year. In some cases, we will ask that students complete StepUp prior to full matriculation. In some cases, we will require ESL (English as a Second Language) courses during matriculation as a student. These decisions are program specific. If you have questions about your individual qualifications, we encourage you to contact the college you are applying to.

Can I waive the English Proficiency exam requirements?
All applicants must exhibit English language proficiency.
Please review our English Proficiency Requirements.
Can I submit self-reported scores with my application?
Yes, self reported scores can be submitted. Official scores will be required for your application to be complete.
How can I submit my official test scores?
Different tests have different submission processes. We have provided some details below, but do not hesitate to contact college office if you have questions.

Transcript Questions
Do I need an official transcript to submit my application?
You can submit an application without an official transcript. Official transcripts will be required if you are admitted to Lehigh.
I am an international student, does my transcript need to be evaluated for equivalency?
International applicants must hold an American bachelor’s degree or the equivalent from a foreign institution of higher education. International applicants applying for regular graduate student status must submit all documents required for that status, as outlined in the respective college’s admission policies. Some colleges may require evaluation.

How can I submit my official transcript?
If you have access to a current version of your unofficial transcript(s) from your prior institution(s), you may upload them to your application and they may be used to review your application. All applicants that accept an offer of admission are required to submit final, official transcripts prior to beginning coursework.
All applicants who accept an offer of admission are required to submit final, official transcripts to maintain enrollment. Applicants must provide transcripts from all institutions from which a degree was earned. Official transcripts are those in a sealed envelope with a degree conferred date and sent directly from the issuing institution to the college mailing address or via e-transcript services to the college.

Other Admissions Requirements Questions
Is an admissions interview offered/required?
In some cases, an admissions interview may be required. If so, the college office will contact you for scheduling.
How can I request a fee waiver?
There are a limited number of fee waivers offered each year. You must start an application in the system to be considered for a fee waiver.
Some general guidelines for fee waivers are as follows:
College of Arts & Sciences: Fee waivers are issued on a limited basis. Please inquire directly with your program of interest.
College of Business: Fee waivers are issued on a limited basis. Contact the college for more information.
College of Education: Fee waivers are issued on a limited basis. Please contact the College of Education to inquire.
P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science: Fee waivers are issued on a limited basis. Please contact the Rossin College to inquire.
College of Health: Fee waivers are issued on a limited basis. Please contact the College of Health to inquire.
